message.content: Painting the Eiffel Tower is a massive undertaking that’s carried out only once every seven years or so. In practice, the actual work—coating the metal lattice with fresh paint—takes roughly **two months**. During that period, crews work around the clock (often 24 hours a day) to apply multiple layers of protective paint to the entire structure, which is about 324 m (1,063 ft) tall and covers an area of roughly 10 000 m² (107 000 ft²). The process is carefully scheduled to avoid disrupting the daily flow of tourists and to ensure the tower’s iconic silhouette remains intact.
